title: Molecular chiral discrimination through symmetry-breaking spin dynamics
authors: Tianyu Xie, Yucheng Hao, Mingzhe Liu, Mengqi Wang, Shaoyi Xu, Zhiyuan Zhao, Chang-Kui Duan, Ya Wang, Fazhan Shi, Jiangfeng Du
abstract: Molecular chirality plays a crucial role in physics, chemistry, life sciences and pharmacology. Nowadays, the chiral discrimination and control at the single-molecule level is urgently needed to reveal the origin of the chirality-relevant phenomena by recovering the information disturbed by the ensemble averaging. The method of magnetic resonance (MR), as one of powerful tools for structure analysis, is blind to the molecular chirality in the absence of a chiral reagent. Here we propose and experimentally demonstrate a direct MR-based method for determining the chirality at the single-molecule level through constructing the symmetry-breaking dynamics of nearby nuclear spins. In principle, the mirror asymmetry of two enantiomers in real space is manifested by breaking the joint symmetry of the mirror reflection and time reversal in spin space under spin dynamics. Experimentally, two enantiomers are indistinguishable from the dynamics of strongly-coupled but unpolarized nuclear spins, but diverge evidently in the dynamical results that break the field-inversion symmetry after spins are polarized. Our method and results will benefit the study of chirality-induced properties in the fields of chemistry and biology.
summary: The authors present an MR-based technique to determine the absolute chirality of single molecules by analyzing symmetry-breaking dynamics among coupled nuclear spins. They show that while standard MR spectra are blind to chirality, measuring spin evolution after polarizing the system reveals a unique signature dependent on molecular handedness. This method offers a novel quantum tool for chemistry and biology.
main_problem: The primary goal is to achieve direct molecular chiral discrimination at the single-molecule level using magnetic resonance (MR) spectroscopy.
main_result: Chirality is successfully determined by observing how the spin dynamics diverge when the system transitions from unpolarized to partially polarized states, breaking the joint symmetry of mirror reflection and time reversal in spin space.
method: The method involves constructing and analyzing the symmetry-breaking dynamics of nearby nuclear spins coupled to an electron spin using single-molecule MR techniques.
model_or_system: The system utilizes Nitrogen-Vacancy (NV) centers in diamond, probing the quantum three-body dynamics of coupled $^{13}	ext{C}$ nuclear spins. The analysis involves Hamiltonian modeling and measuring coherence under dynamical decoupling sequences.
key_observables: Chirality-related phases ($\Phi(ij)$), population differences ($P|_{+angle} - P_{|0angle}$), and the deviation of spin dynamics from unpolarized expectations.
important_parameters: Electron spin gap ($\Delta$), magnetic field strength, and hyperfine coupling parameters derived from DFT calculations.
main_assumptions: The method assumes that molecular chirality manifests as a breaking of MT-symmetry in the measured spin dynamics when polarization is induced.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy spectra comparison (Fig. 1(c)), dynamical profiles showing divergence upon polarization (Figs. 2, 3), and methods for determining NV axis direction using electric fields (Fig. S8).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the need for chiral discrimination to detailing the MR-based measurement technique, analyzing two-body and then three-body spin dynamics under varying polarization levels, and finally confirming the results via field reversal and comparison with theoretical calculations.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful quantum sensing platform using solid-state defects (NV centers) to probe fundamental symmetries related to molecular structure, bridging quantum information concepts with chirality detection in condensed matter systems.
